plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies tightly curled woolly hair as a cutaneous manifestation of Naxos disease.
Caption explicitly identifies palmar keratoses, and the image shows diffuse thickening and scaling of the palm.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of a patient's tightly curled scalp hair demonstrating the characteristic woolly-hair phenotype of Naxos disease. [raw subtype: Naxos disease] B: Clinical photograph showing diffuse palmar keratoderma, a characteristic cutaneous manifestation of Naxos disease. [raw subtype: Naxos disease] C: Clinical photograph showing diffuse plantar keratoderma, a characteristic cutaneous manifestation of Naxos disease. [raw subtype: Naxos disease]

panels.figure_caption: Cutaneous phenotype of Naxos disease: woolly hair (A), palmar (B) and plantar (C) keratoses.
in_text_mentions: Woolly hair appears from birth, whereas palmoplantar keratoderma develop during the first year of life when infants start to use their hands and feet (Figure 1) [13]. The cardiomyopathy clinically manifests by adolescence and shows 100% penetrance [14]. The symptomatic presentation is usually with syncope and/or sustained ventricular tachycardia of left bundle branch block configuration (Figure 2).
